text:
Winnipeg did most of the work and still lost. The Jets generated 3.63 expected goals to Boston's 3.19 and would have won 55 percent of simulated replays, yet it was JJ Peterka who ended it, snapping a wrist shot 3:21 into overtime off a feed from David Pastrnak and Nikita Zadorov. Boston's 4-3 win came with Jeremy Swayman stopping 30 of 33 chances worth 3.47 expected goals, a small edge of 0.47 saved above expected, while Stuart Skinner allowed four on 3.19 expected.

The Jets did their damage in bursts and in the margins. Dylan DeMelo's slap shot opened the scoring from a 2 percent chance, and Mario Ferraro's wrist shot in the final seconds of the second period, a 1 percent look, put Winnipeg up 3-2. Kyle Connor tied it on the power play and finished with nine shots and 1.14 individual expected goals, the most dangerous player on the ice. Even so, Boston was better at even strength, 2.61 expected goals to 1.96, so Winnipeg's edge came from special teams and volume of chances in the middle period (1.23 to 0.97).

Boston earned its escape late. Hampus Lindholm tied the game in the first, James Hagens put the Bruins up with a 35 percent chance, and Elias Lindholm tipped in the equalizer with 1:38 left in regulation. Pastrnak was in the middle of it all, with two assists in 22 minutes. The Bruins also blocked 20 shots to Winnipeg's 13, which helped them survive a game the numbers say they were slightly lucky to win.
